title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering to prevent regional failover thrashing
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: In production we've observed repeated regional failover 'thrashing' during transient upstream congestion: the SLO enforcer would trigger backoff on several nodes simultaneously, ordering/backoff decisions would race, and regions would repeatedly drop into load-shedding and then immediately attempt failback. This caused user-visible elevated error rates and capacity oscillation. Root cause: non-deterministic ordering in the backoff decision path and a missing global jitter/window that coordinates regional cooldowns. This PR implements a low-risk hotfix that makes backoff ordering deterministic, adds a coordinated cooldown window with jitter, and tightens the enforcer's priority queue semantics to prevent rapid re-entry into failover state. Goals: make a targeted change that is safe for rolling deploy to Dedicated and Hosted, with minimal behavior change outside of preventing failback thrash, add telemetry to validate in canary, and include tests that reproduce the race. Changes in this PR: - Make SLO enforcer backoff ordering deterministic by using a stable sort on (priority, last_decision_ts) and ensuring decisions are applied under the same compare function across nodes. - Introduce a regional-cooldown window (configurable, default 30s) and randomized jitter (0-5s) to stagger re-enable attempts across nodes. - Prevent immediate re-enqueue of previously shed requests by tracking short-lived token-level backoff markers (in-memory, TTLed) to avoid looped shedding on bursts. - Fix priority-queue comparator bug that allowed lower-priority queues to preempt higher-priority backoff under certain races. - Add metrics: slo_enforcer.backoff_decision{reason,region}, slo_enforcer.cooldown_start, slo_enforcer.cooldown_end, slo_enforcer.jitter_applied and histograms for decision_latency. - Add unit tests replicating the race, and an integration test for regional cooldown behavior. - Add a feature-flag guarded rollout (FEATURE_SLO_ENFORCER_STABLE_BACKOFF) so we can canary in production. Checklist: - [x] Implement deterministic ordering and cooldown window - [x] Add metrics and logs for validation - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add feature flag and config with sane defaults - [x] Run canary against a subset of regions and validate metrics - [x] Roll out to main with gradual percent rollout Related: Linear ENG-5123 (SLO enforcer stability), ENG-5180 (regional failover investigation). Support ticket SUP-2345 reported customer-facing errors during the incident.

ci_checks: CI: e2e (flaky) - skipped for hotfix, will run during canary
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering, add regional cooldown with jitter, prevent failback thrashing. Rollout guarded by FEATURE_SLO_ENFORCER_STABLE_BACKOFF. Metrics added for validation.
deployment_notes: Canary rollout plan: enable feature flag in 5% of traffic in one region for 30 minutes, confirm slo_enforcer.backoff_decision and cooldown metrics show reduced oscillation, then ramp 25/50/100. If errors increase, revert flag. Config knobs: slo_enforcer.cooldown_window (default 30s), slo_enforcer.jitter_max_ms (default 5000).
post_deploy_validation: Use the dashboard observability/dashboards/slo-enforcer.json and check metrics: decrease in repeated backoff_count per region and lower decision_latency variance. Pager policy: SEV2 if failover oscillates >3 times in 5 minutes after rollout.
